summary.text: St. Mel was an early bishop of Ardagh, associated with St. Patrick’s mission and with St. Brigid’s religious profession.

blocks.text: St. Mel is remembered as the founder and first bishop of Ardagh. Irish genealogies connect him to St. Patrick’s family, but the historical reference treats such family traditions as transmitted material rather than a securely reconstructed modern biography.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The early collection of traditions attributed to Tírechán says that St. Patrick ordained him bishop. A later Life places his foundation at Ardagh in the kingdom of Tethbae. Accounts concerning St. Brigid say that she received the veil before him. These different texts preserve the relationships for which he is most often mentioned in introductions to early Irish Christianity.

blocks.text: The cited reference places his death in 487 and connects February 6 with the martyrologies. It does not establish the medical cause or an execution. Stories about miraculous vindication and rescue belong to later hagiographical narratives and are not necessary to identify his episcopal ministry.
